EQUITY_NARRATIVE: 131 The Point Drive was previously listed at $3,250,000 by Ben Bowen in March 2025 and withdrawn after 103 days in June. At $526/SF, the home is priced above the area's average closed price of $438/SF. A modest price adjustment to $3,199,000 would bring the $/SF closer to market norms and provide a fresh start with improved market positioning. With a deeded boat slip, golf course views, and premium Simonini construction, the home's fundamentals are strong — the opportunity is in strategic repositioning.
SOLD_RADIUS_DESC: Within 0.5 Miles of 131 The Point Drive · The Point Subdivision · Last 365 Days
CLOSED_COMPS_ANALYSIS: The strongest closed comp is 130 Brick Kiln Way — a 4/6, 5,744 SF waterfront property with 250+ ft of shoreline and a private beach that sold for $3,730,000 ($650/SF) in just 24 days. Notably, it had no pool (only renderings) and came off the market quickly due to its exceptional waterfront position. This sets a ceiling for premium waterfront product. Non-waterfront and less premium properties in The Point have closed in the $1–2M range, underscoring the premium buyers assign to direct water access.
PENDING_RADIUS_DESC: Within 0.5 Miles of 131 The Point Drive · Currently Under Contract
PENDING_COMPS_ANALYSIS: 105 Moors End Loop — a 4/7, 7,190 SF waterfront home with dock and pool — went under contract in 21 days at $4,975,000 ($692/SF). This confirms strong buyer demand for fully-loaded waterfront product with pool and dock at the $4.5M–$5M range. The premium over 131 The Point is justified by direct waterfront access, dock, and pool — all features buyers in this market prioritize.

RECOMMENDATION_TEXT: List at $3,199,000. This represents a modest adjustment from the prior list price of $3,250,000 — enough to signal a fresh start to buyers who may have dismissed the property, without conceding significant value. At $518/SF, the home is priced competitively against its waterfront competitors and below the area's active median. The deeded boat slip, Simonini construction quality, and golf course views are compelling differentiators that need the right price to convert showings to offers.
BOTTOM_LINE_TEXT: The buyer pool at $3M+ is notably thinner — showings at the $2.1M range average 13, while $3M+ homes typically see a maximum of 3 showings. This is expected at the luxury level, but sets the stage: every showing is high-stakes, and pricing needs to convert. A $3,199,000 list price provides the best balance of perceived value, competitive positioning, and realistic path to contract.
